Alex.confusing: The dead-player rules were the hardest to track: I had to remember that my throws still scored but my votes didn't count. The egg-token timing (tokens cashed only after the vote) also took some sorting out.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when Drew's Owl, Finley, and Alex stories kept shifting and the table turned on Drew together. Drew was the Sphinx, so the read was right.
Alex.change: I'd make the day's CAW CAW and vote timing clearer, since the day ended after only three beats with some players still unheard.
Alex.regret: None that I'd change much: my Round 3 Hawk read on Ellis was correct and I banked 25 points from it. I could have spoken earlier about Blair's Owl-to-Hawk role change to test it sooner.

Blair.confusing: The night-visit rules are hard to track, especially Owl, Turkey and Kookaburra, since a visit can add an egg to the visitor, the target, or cause confusion. Drew's Turkey and Owl claims were the hardest to check.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when Drew's story kept changing from Finley to Alex and the table lined up to vote them out. Their Owl, Finley, and Alex claims kept collapsing on each other.
Blair.change: I would make it clearer when a visit is confirmed by a dawn report, since players often can't tell whether a claim is true or a bluff. I'd also make the score-pile rule easier to read at a glance.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I was confident Ellis was Meowfia but threw only two low cards (D2 and W3) for 2 points, keeping my S11 and H8 worth just 1 each at the end. I should have thrown high cards like S11 when confident, since banked cards score at full value.

Casey.confusing: The Turkey rule was unclear: it's hard to tell whether the egg lands in the Turkey's nest or the visitor's, and that confusion drove most of the day arguments in round 2.
Casey.fun: Round 3 was fun: as Mouser I winked at Alex, and the table tried to read Ellis and Drew while the real Sphinx sat in plain sight.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn reports say whose visit caused each egg change, so players can check claims without guessing which animal does what.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I claimed to be an Owl and invented a visit to Drew, which was an easy lie to catch. I should have stayed quiet or claimed a role that didn't depend on an egg change I couldn't back up.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey rule was easy to misread: several players, me included, got tangled over whether a visitor gains an egg in the Turkey's nest or the Turkey gains one. Nest-count evidence also got confusing once roles swapped between rounds.
Drew.fun: Round 3 was satisfying: my Kookaburra visit exposed Ellis as the Sphinx, and the table lined up behind that read to eggsecute them.
Drew.change: I would make the day's claims and egg-count evidence easier to check, for example by having the Storyteller state each visitor and egg change publicly.
Drew.regret: In Round 2, as Meowfia Sphinx, I made up a Finley visit and then changed it to Alex, which made my story look shaky. I should have stayed quiet or kept one consistent, plausible claim.

Ellis.confusing: The Eggsecution tie rule and how thrown cards come back were hard to track, especially the consolation for throwing at the other team. It was also unclear whether a Turkey's visitor egg lands in the visitor's nest or the Turkey's, which caused a lot of dispute on day 2.
Ellis.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: as the Sphinx I had to bluff as an Owl and defend against Drew's Kookaburra claim while the table pushed me, and the day votes turned on who was lying.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn reports and claimed egg effects easier to cross-check, so players can tell at a glance whether a visit or a Turkey egg really happened.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I threw a Wild and stayed quiet, which hid me but gave the table no real information. Next time I'd make an earlier, clearer claim about my Mouser visit to steer the vote toward Casey sooner.

Finley.confusing: The Kookaburra rule was unclear: a visit only confuses you if someone visited you, so I couldn't tell whether a visitor claim was true without checking my dawn report. Several players also mixed up which animal gave which egg, like the Turkey and Hawk.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when my Kookaburra visit to Drew revealed the Sphinx and the table turned on Drew's shifting Owl, Turkey and Alex stories.
Finley.change: I'd make it clearer when a dawn report shows a role change or confusion, so players can check claims without guessing.
Finley.regret: I threw only low cards (W6, C3, W4, H5) in my winning rounds, banking just 3 and 5 points, when I could have thrown higher cards to score more. I'd throw my higher cards once I was confident in the Meowfia read.

review.title: Three Easy Hunts
review.headline: Meowfia got caught three times running, and the table never really doubted it.
review.summary: Each round the table piled onto one player within a few beats, and that player was Meowfia every time. Casey and Drew were undone by claims that clashed with a Turkey or Kookaburra report. In round 3 Ellis was exposed by a Hawk egg and a Kookaburra read, even though Casey's Wink killed the Hawk. Alex won the game by banking 25 points in round 3, as a dead player who still threw his two best cards.

rounds.recap: Blair's Hawk egg pointed at Casey, the Sphinx. Casey bluffed Owl and said he visited Drew. Drew was a Turkey with no egg, so the lie failed at once. Farm agreed and called CAW by beat 3. Casey was eggsecuted and Farm won.

Finley's Kookaburra read named Drew as Sphinx in beat 1. Drew's Owl story then changed twice, and he misstated how the Turkey works. Everyone threw at Drew and Farm won. Ellis banked 13 points and took the lead.

Alex's Hawk egg pointed at Ellis. Casey winked Alex, but Drew's Kookaburra read had already named Ellis as Sphinx. Blair's Owl read and Finley's Falcon read backed it up. Casey and Ellis split their throws and Ellis was eggsecuted. Alex was dead but banked 25 points and won the game.

highlights.text: Casey claimed Owl and said he visited Drew. Drew's Turkey had no egg, so the lie was exposed in beat 1.
Drew moved his visit from Finley to Alex and then misstated the Turkey rule, which sealed his fate.
Casey winked Alex, the Hawk accuser, mid-day. It did not save Ellis, because Drew's Kookaburra read had already named him as Sphinx.
Dead Alex threw H12 and H13 at Ellis and banked 25 points. That won him the game.

confusions.what: Said the Turkey lays the egg in the visitor's nest. The Turkey's own nest gains.
Claimed an Owl visit to a Turkey and a no-egg result. Owl lays an egg only if no one else visited, and a Turkey would have given him an egg.
Asked whether a Kookaburra is confused by their own visit. Only a visit to the Kookaburra confuses them, so a clean report means nobody visited.
Said 'Mouser-less so far' in a garbled bluff. He gave an incoherent non-claim.
Said an Owl nest wouldn't gain if visited, and asked Blair why a Sphinx visit was no egg. This confused the Owl and Hawk rules.
Threw at Drew, a likely Farm player, because he thought Ellis was his partner. Meowfia can't know this, and the throw failed.

worked: Hawk eggs and Turkey or Kookaburra reports gave hard facts that could be cross-checked. Casey's and Drew's lies collapsed against them.
The Wink in round 3 was a bold play. Killing the accuser mid-day gave a real tactical moment.
Dead players still throw cards and can still score. Alex's 25-point round made the endgame scoring interesting.
Scoring by throw value gave the final standings real swings, such as Ellis's 13 in round 2 and Alex's 25 in round 3.
problems: Farm solved every round in beat 1 or 2. Information roles (Hawk, Kookaburra, Falcon, Owl) are too strong against Meowfia, so tension was low. Fix: give Meowfia more cover, or reduce reliable reads.

Meowfia don't know each other, so they can't coordinate. They threw at each other and lost three times. The partner-guessing in round 3 was a mistake, not a decision. Fix: give some cats a way to find partners.
The Wink did not matter in round 3. A kill that also leaves the target's score pile intact is weak. Fix: let a killed player lose their vote and their throw.

Throw size is the main scoring tool, but almost everyone just threw low cards at the consensus target. Safe low throws and a floor of kept cards made the vote a formality. Fix: make a win bonus scale with the number of cards thrown.
Turkey and Owl rules are hard to follow. Several players misread them or the egg token flow. Fix: clearer wording on who gains the egg.
